findings.failure_path: Once the transcript passes 20,000 events or 16 MB, or has any line over 1 MB, the helper returns an error. The gate then prints only an 'unverified' message and never blocks, even for edits that appear early in the scanned part. A long session, or one large tool output, turns the extraction backstop into a non-blocking message. Previously the gate still blocked on edits found in the scanned head.
findings.smallest_fix: When truncated, still output edit_paths found in the scanned prefix, or scan the tail. Keep blocking on those edits and add the 'unverified' note. Add a test where an edit appears before the padding and must still block.

findings.failure_path: The new goal race test expects a deny and no leftover sentinel. However, the guard and prompt code for goal grants (epoch check after mv, consume, revoke) is not in this packet. The claim that goal revocation cannot bring a grant back rests only on this test and on reviews outside the packet.
findings.smallest_fix: Add the guard-merge-authorization.sh and merge-authorization-prompt.sh diffs to the release review packet, or record the reviewed commit hash that this delta builds on.

concern_results.conclusion: The delta fixes the earlier P1s. With Python missing, Claude single-path edits are checked through jq again, and apply_patch still fails closed. Owner-dispatch now inspects every target, so a deny beats an advisory. Oversized startup text is reported and never cut, and same-version install reuses doctor's message. I found no remaining P0 or P1 in this delta. One P2 remains: once a transcript passes the scan limit, the extraction Stop gate no longer blocks at all.

The guard now checks all targets and has no advisory short-circuit, and the no-Python fallback is tested for each tool and for relative paths. The new goal race test covers revoke and scope change during consume, but the guard code it exercises is not in this packet. That authorization proof rests on an earlier partition review; this delta alone cannot confirm it.
